49.text:
Large cities offer opportunities and excitement, but many of them also suffer from high levels of theft, violence and drug-related crime. This essay will analyse the principal causes and propose realistic solutions.

Crime in large cities is driven by inequality, unemployment and weak social ties. Where some people see wealth around them but have no job or prospects, and where neighbours do not know one another, gangs, drugs and theft become more attractive and harder to detect. A teenager who leaves school with no qualifications and no job, for example, may be drawn by a gang that offers money and belonging. In addition, crowded housing, poor schools and the easy availability of drugs and alcohol increase the risk, and the anonymity of city life makes offenders feel safe from being recognised. Families may also be under strain, leaving young people with little guidance. As a result, crime tends to concentrate in a few deprived districts.

To address this issue, governments should tackle the causes of crime as well as punish offenders. Jobs, education and youth programmes give people a stake in society, better lighting and street design make public places safer, and treatment for addiction reduces the crimes that feed it. In addition, community policing, in which officers get to know the residents they serve, helps to build trust and gives early warning of problems. Faster and fairer courts, together with support for former prisoners to find work, reduce reoffending. These measures cost less than building more prisons, and the improvement lasts longer.

In conclusion, crime in large cities stems mainly from inequality, unemployment and weak community ties, but investment in opportunity, safer design and community policing offers a realistic way forward.

90.text:
In several countries, serious crimes involving firearms regularly make the news, and some argue that stricter gun control reduces crime. I largely agree, since fewer guns make violence less deadly, although gun control alone cannot remove crime.

To begin with, stricter gun control makes violent crime less deadly. Fewer guns in circulation and checks on buyers make it harder for dangerous people to obtain weapons and reduce deaths in arguments and accidents. An argument between neighbours, for example, is far less likely to end in a death if neither has easy access to a gun. Countries with strict licensing, background checks and limits on ownership, such as Japan and the United Kingdom, tend to have far fewer gun deaths than countries where guns are widely available. Gun control also reduces suicides and accidental shootings, which make up a large share of firearm deaths.

Furthermore, controls make it harder for criminals to arm themselves, since many illegal guns begin as legal ones that were stolen or sold carelessly. However, gun control has limits. Determined criminals can still find illegal guns, particularly where borders are open and black markets are well established, and strict laws are of little use if they are not enforced. Crime also has other causes, such as poverty, drugs and gangs, which require different solutions. Gun laws should therefore be accompanied by tracing of weapons, penalties for illegal sales, and programmes that tackle gangs and unemployment. Public support for the laws and clear rules for lawful owners, such as hunters, also make them easier to apply.

In conclusion, stricter gun control reduces crime and deaths to a large extent, but it works best as part of a wider strategy against violence.

91.text:
Opinions are divided as to whether public money should be spent mainly on policing or on social services. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of policing argue that police respond to crime at once. Officers deter offenders, protect victims and catch criminals, and the presence of patrols makes residents feel safe enough to go out, shop and invest in their neighbourhood. A town with regular patrols, for example, tends to experience fewer break-ins and less vandalism, and a quick response can save lives when violence occurs. Residents who feel secure are more likely to work, trade and send their children to school, so safety is the foundation of everyday life. Police also deal with emergencies that no other service can handle, from road accidents to terrorism.

On the other hand, supporters of social services point out that they help to prevent crime by dealing with its causes. Jobs, mental health care, housing support and youth services reduce the pressures that lead people to crime in the first place, and they cost far less than arrests, trials and prison sentences. A young person who is helped into training, for instance, is less likely to join a gang and may become a taxpayer instead of an offender. Social services also help victims and reduce reoffending, so their effect lasts longer than short-term deterrence. However, their results take years to appear, and the public often demands visible action.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Overall, I believe that a balanced budget gives the best results, with enough police to ensure immediate safety and a growing share for social services that prevent crime in the long term.

Phòng tội phạm bằng giải quyết nguyên nhân: việc làm, chăm sóc tâm thần, nhà ở, dịch vụ thanh niên; rẻ hơn bắt giữ, xét xử, tù; ví dụ thanh niên được đào tạo ít vào băng nhóm. Giúp nạn nhân, giảm tái phạm; nhưng kết quả mất nhiều năm, công chúng đòi hành động thấy được.

130.text:
Politicians often respond to rising crime by promising longer sentences, and some argue that harsher penalties reduce crime. I agree only to a limited extent, since the certainty of being caught deters more than the severity of the sentence, although serious offenders must be kept from harming others.

To begin with, the certainty of being caught deters crime more than the severity of the sentence. Offenders rarely expect to be caught, so longer sentences have little effect on their decisions. A thief who believes that he will probably not be caught, for example, is hardly influenced by whether the maximum sentence is five or ten years. Many crimes are committed on impulse, under the influence of drugs or alcohol, or in anger, when people do not think about penalties at all. Studies in several countries suggest that visible policing and a high chance of arrest do more to prevent crime than heavier punishment.

Furthermore, harsh penalties have costs. Prisons are expensive, overcrowded and often teach new crimes to those who enter them, so released prisoners may commit more offences, and long sentences leave families without support. However, penalties are not meaningless. Serious and violent offenders need long sentences to protect the public, and clear punishments express society's disapproval and give justice to victims. The strongest approach combines a high chance of detection, swift and fair trials, proportionate sentences and rehabilitation, such as education and job training in prison. This reduces reoffending more effectively than severity alone. Resources spent on police and courts are therefore often better value than extra years in prison.

In conclusion, harsher penalties reduce crime only to a limited extent, because deterrence depends more on certainty than severity, though serious crimes still require firm punishment.

175.text:
In some countries the state may execute people convicted of the most serious crimes, and some believe that the death penalty deters crime. I disagree with this view, since there is no clear evidence that it works better than long imprisonment, and the risks of the punishment are very high.

To begin with, there is no clear evidence that the death penalty deters crime better than long imprisonment. Many serious crimes are committed in anger or without expecting capture, so offenders do not weigh the penalty at all. Comparisons between regions with and without the death penalty have not shown consistently lower murder rates in the places that execute criminals. Terrorists and organised criminals may even welcome martyrdom. What deters most offenders is the fear of being caught, not the exact punishment that follows. In practice, the death penalty is also rarely applied, which weakens any threat that it might carry.

Furthermore, the punishment is irreversible. Courts sometimes make mistakes, and a man who is executed and later proved innocent, for example, cannot be given back his life. Evidence suggests that poor defendants and members of minority groups are more likely to be sentenced to death, which raises serious concerns about fairness. Many people also believe that the state should not take life, and the costs of lengthy appeals can exceed those of life imprisonment. Supporters argue that the death penalty gives justice to victims and permanently protects society. However, life imprisonment without release also protects the public, while allowing mistakes to be corrected.

In conclusion, I disagree that the death penalty deters crime, because the evidence is weak and the risk of executing the innocent is too serious to accept.

181.text:
After every violent incident involving young people, someone blames video games, and some people say that they promote violence. I disagree with this view, since the evidence that games cause real violence is weak, and other factors matter far more.

To begin with, evidence that video games cause real violence is weak. Hundreds of millions of people play violent games without harming anyone, and violent crime has fallen in several countries as gaming has grown. A teenager who plays a shooting game with friends in the evening, for example, usually treats it as entertainment, as he would a film. Large studies have found, at most, small and short-lived increases in aggression after playing, comparable to those after watching a competitive sport. Most players understand that what happens on a screen is fiction and have no wish to copy it, and many games involve cooperation, planning and creativity.

Furthermore, real violence has far more serious causes. Family background, poverty, abuse, mental illness, drug use and access to weapons are much stronger predictors, and blaming games distracts attention from these problems. When a violent offender happens to play games, this reflects how common games are among young people, not that they caused the crime. However, games are not harmless for everyone. Very young children should not play adult games, extreme content may disturb vulnerable players, and long hours of play can affect sleep and school work. Parents should check age ratings, set time limits and talk to children about what they play. These practical steps are more effective than blaming the medium.

In conclusion, I disagree that video games promote violence, because the evidence is weak and other factors matter more, though sensible limits for children are wise.

analysis.type_vi: Agree/Disagree: trò chơi điện tử khuyến khích bạo lực — disagree

Hàng trăm triệu người chơi không hại ai; tội phạm bạo lực giảm ở nhiều nước khi chơi game tăng. Ví dụ thiếu niên chơi game bắn súng với bạn buổi tối xem như giải trí. Nghiên cứu lớn chỉ thấy tăng hung hăng nhỏ, ngắn; người chơi hiểu đó là hư cấu; nhiều game cần hợp tác, lập kế hoạch, sáng tạo.

plan.step: 3. Lý do 2 — nguyên nhân thật + nhượng bộ

Nhượng bộ: không vô hại với mọi người: trẻ nhỏ không nên chơi game người lớn, nội dung cực đoan, chơi nhiều giờ ảnh hưởng ngủ và học; cha mẹ xem phân loại độ tuổi, đặt giới hạn thời gian, trò chuyện.

272.text:
Millions of people have had their names, bank details or passwords stolen and used by criminals, and opinions differ on who should be responsible for preventing identity theft. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of personal responsibility argue that individuals can do a great deal to protect themselves. People can use strong and different passwords, avoid clicking on suspicious links, check their bank statements regularly and shred documents that contain personal details. A person who receives an email that appears to come from the bank, for example, may give away passwords unless he or she has been warned about such tricks. Careful behaviour online, such as limiting the information shared on social media, makes it harder for criminals to impersonate someone. Since criminals rely on carelessness, a cautious public is the first line of defence.

On the other hand, advocates of action by society and government point out that individuals cannot protect data they do not control. Banks, retailers and online services store enormous amounts of information, and a single hack can expose millions of customers. Only these organisations can secure their systems, and only governments can pass laws that require companies to protect data, punish offenders and cooperate across borders to catch them. Police need specialist skills and international agreements to trace criminals who operate from other countries. Victims, meanwhile, often spend months repairing their records, and they need legal support and quick routes to restore their identity.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Overall, I believe that the most effective approach combines official leadership with personal action, since institutions must secure data and punish criminals while individuals take sensible precautions.

analysis.type_vi: Discuss both views: ngăn chặn trộm danh tính — cá nhân hay xã hội / chính phủ

plan.step: 1. Khung hai quan điểm (dùng lại mô hình 'cá nhân vs chính phủ' đã dùng ở môi trường và y tế)
plan.think: Mở bài nêu thực tế (hàng triệu người bị lấy tên, thông tin ngân hàng, mật khẩu); mỗi thân bài một phía; kết luận kết hợp.

Mật khẩu mạnh khác nhau, tránh nhấp liên kết đáng ngờ, kiểm tra sao kê, huỷ tài liệu có thông tin; ví dụ người nhận email giả ngân hàng có thể đưa mật khẩu nếu chưa được cảnh báo; hạn chế chia sẻ trên mạng xã hội; công chúng thận trọng là tuyến phòng thủ đầu tiên.

Cá nhân không bảo vệ được dữ liệu mình không kiểm soát: ngân hàng, cửa hàng, dịch vụ trực tuyến lưu lượng thông tin khổng lồ; một vụ tấn công làm lộ hàng triệu khách; chỉ tổ chức này bảo mật hệ thống; chính phủ ra luật, trừng phạt, hợp tác xuyên biên giới; nạn nhân cần hỗ trợ pháp lý.
Kết hợp: tổ chức bảo mật dữ liệu và trừng phạt tội phạm; cá nhân thận trọng.

292.text:
When a crime shocks the public, people ask whether it is the result of social conditions or of a wrong choice, and opinions are divided as to whether crime is mainly caused by poverty and lack of education or whether criminals are personally responsible. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, those who blame social conditions argue that poverty and poor education raise the risk of crime. People with no job and no prospects face stronger temptation and fewer legitimate options, and schools in poor areas may fail to give children the skills they need. A teenager who leaves school with no qualifications and no job, for example, may be drawn by a gang that offers money and belonging. Studies often show that crime rates are higher in deprived districts, where unemployment, poor housing and family breakdown combine. From this point of view, improving schools and creating jobs would reduce crime more effectively than punishment.

On the other hand, supporters of personal responsibility point out that poverty does not excuse crime. Most poor people obey the law, and crime also occurs among the wealthy, for example in fraud and corruption. Every offender makes a choice, and treating criminals as victims of circumstance can weaken respect for the law and ignore the harm done to real victims. Courts should therefore hold people accountable for their actions. A person who steals when he could have asked for help, for instance, has made a decision that others in the same position avoided. Accountability also gives offenders the dignity of being treated as responsible adults.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Personally, I believe that social conditions raise the risk of crime, but individuals remain responsible for their choices, so both opportunity and accountability must be addressed.

analysis.type_vi: Discuss both views: tội phạm chủ yếu do nghèo và thiếu giáo dục hay do trách nhiệm cá nhân

plan.think: Mở bài nêu câu hỏi chung (do hoàn cảnh xã hội hay lựa chọn sai) rồi hai phe; ý kiến riêng kết hợp: hoàn cảnh nâng rủi ro nhưng cá nhân vẫn chịu trách nhiệm.

Nghèo và giáo dục kém tăng rủi ro: người không việc, không triển vọng đối mặt cám dỗ mạnh, ít lựa chọn hợp pháp; trường ở khu nghèo không đủ kỹ năng. Ví dụ thiếu niên bị băng nhóm lôi kéo. Nghiên cứu cho thấy tội phạm cao ở khu nghèo; cải thiện trường học và việc làm hiệu quả hơn trừng phạt.

Nghèo không biện minh cho tội phạm: đa số người nghèo tuân thủ luật; tội phạm cũng xảy ra ở người giàu (gian lận, tham nhũng); mỗi người phạm tội đều lựa chọn; coi tội phạm là nạn nhân hoàn cảnh làm yếu sự tôn trọng pháp luật và bỏ qua nạn nhân thật. Ví dụ người trộm thay vì xin giúp. Trách nhiệm cho người phạm tội phẩm giá của người trưởng thành có trách nhiệm.
Hoàn cảnh nâng rủi ro nhưng cá nhân vẫn chịu trách nhiệm; cần giải quyết cả cơ hội và trách nhiệm giải trình.

293.text:
When crime rises, governments face a choice between preventing it and punishing it, and some people prefer crime prevention measures while others prefer stricter punishments. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of prevention argue that stopping crime before it happens is cheaper and kinder than dealing with its consequences. Better street lighting, security cameras, youth programmes, drug treatment and job training reduce the opportunities and pressures that lead people to offend. A neighbourhood with a youth club and well-lit streets, for example, may see fewer incidents because young people have somewhere to go and offenders feel watched. Preventing a crime also saves the victim from suffering, and costs far less than arrests, trials and prison. Prevention can also strengthen communities, since residents who feel responsible for their area tend to look out for one another.

On the other hand, supporters of stricter punishment emphasise justice and protection. Offenders who harm others should be held accountable, and firm penalties show victims that society takes their suffering seriously. Long sentences keep dangerous people away from the public, and the prospect of a heavy penalty may deter some people from offending. Prevention is slow and uncertain, and people who have decided to commit a serious crime may not be influenced by programmes. A violent offender who is released early and attacks again, for instance, shows the cost of lenient treatment. Many citizens want to see visible consequences for wrongdoing.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Personally, I believe that prevention should receive greater emphasis because it is more effective in the long term, while proportionate punishment remains necessary for serious crimes.

analysis.type_vi: Discuss both views: biện pháp phòng ngừa tội phạm hay trừng phạt nghiêm khắc hơn

plan.think: Mở bài nêu lựa chọn của chính phủ khi tội phạm tăng (phòng hay phạt); mỗi thân bài một phía; ý kiến riêng nghiêng về phòng ngừa nhưng giữ trừng phạt cho tội nghiêm trọng.

Ngăn tội phạm trước khi xảy ra rẻ và nhân văn hơn; đèn đường, camera, chương trình thanh niên, điều trị ma tuý, đào tạo nghề giảm cơ hội và áp lực; ví dụ khu phố có câu lạc bộ thanh niên và đèn sáng ít sự cố hơn; bảo vệ nạn nhân khỏi đau khổ; củng cố cộng đồng.

Công lý và bảo vệ: người hại người khác phải chịu trách nhiệm; hình phạt cứng rắn cho nạn nhân thấy xã hội coi trọng đau khổ của họ; án dài giữ người nguy hiểm xa công chúng; răn đe một số người. Phòng ngừa chậm và không chắc; người đã quyết phạm tội nặng có thể không bị chương trình ảnh hưởng. Ví dụ kẻ bạo lực được thả sớm tấn công lần nữa.
Nhấn mạnh phòng ngừa vì hiệu quả dài hạn, trừng phạt tương xứng cho tội nghiêm trọng.

305.text:
Laws work only when people obey them and when someone enforces them, and opinions differ on whether individuals should be responsible for upholding the law or whether society and government should take primary responsibility. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of individual responsibility argue that a law is only as strong as the willingness of citizens to follow it. Most laws are obeyed voluntarily, since people pay taxes, drive within limits and respect others' property without any officer watching them, and police could never monitor everyone all the time. Citizens who report crimes, serve on juries and refuse to take part in dishonest practices make the system work. A driver who stops at a red light on an empty road, for example, shows a respect for rules that no number of cameras could produce. A society in which people obey the law only from fear of punishment would be unstable and costly to run.

On the other hand, advocates of government responsibility point out that individuals cannot enforce laws themselves. Only the state can make fair laws, investigate crimes, bring suspects to court and punish offenders in a way that is lawful and consistent. Private individuals who take the law into their own hands risk violence, mistakes and revenge. Governments must also ensure that laws are clear, that police act fairly and that courts are independent, so that people trust the system and are willing to cooperate. An angry crowd that punishes a suspected thief, for instance, shows what can happen without proper institutions.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Overall, I believe that governments should take primary responsibility for making and enforcing laws, while individuals support them by obeying them and cooperating with the authorities.

analysis.type_vi: Discuss both views: cá nhân hay xã hội / chính phủ chịu trách nhiệm chính về thực thi pháp luật

plan.think: Mở bài nêu nguyên lý (luật chỉ có tác dụng khi được tuân thủ và có người thực thi) rồi hai phe; ý kiến riêng chính phủ chịu trách nhiệm chính, cá nhân hỗ trợ.

Luật mạnh bằng sự sẵn lòng tuân thủ của công dân: phần lớn luật được tuân thủ tự nguyện (đóng thuế, lái xe trong giới hạn, tôn trọng tài sản); cảnh sát không thể giám sát mọi người; báo tội phạm, làm bồi thẩm, từ chối gian lận. Ví dụ tài xế dừng đèn đỏ trên đường vắng. Xã hội chỉ tuân thủ vì sợ phạt sẽ bất ổn, tốn kém.

Cá nhân không tự thực thi luật: chỉ nhà nước ban hành luật công bằng, điều tra, đưa ra toà, trừng phạt hợp pháp và nhất quán; cá nhân tự xử gây bạo lực, sai lầm, trả thù; chính phủ đảm bảo luật rõ, cảnh sát công bằng, toà độc lập để dân tin và hợp tác. Ví dụ đám đông giận dữ trừng phạt nghi phạm.
Chính phủ chịu trách nhiệm chính; cá nhân hỗ trợ bằng tuân thủ và hợp tác.
